title: Luxury Café Furniture Configurator
description: Users configure a premium café seating vignette by positioning a damask purple-gold chair and coffee mat on a showroom floor. They adjust material properties, lighting mood, and arrangement to create a product showcase scene, then export a final camera angle for a catalog shot.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a luxury café furniture product configurator. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader: 'shared_assets/coffeemat.glb' (a coffee mat/placemat) and 'shared_assets/ChairDamaskPurplegold.glb' (an ornate damask purple-gold chair). Place them on a reflective circular showroom platform (MeshStandardMaterial with metalness 0.3, roughness 0.2, color #2a2a2a). The chair starts at center, the coffee mat starts offset to the right. Camera uses OrbitControls starting at position (3, 2.5, 3) looking at origin. Add a warm key light (DirectionalLight, intensity 1.5, color #fff5e6), a cool fill light (color #c8d8ff, intensity 0.6), and ambient light (intensity 0.3). Implement these interaction steps with validation: (1) A draggable gizmo system using raycasting — click an object to select it (highlight with emissive outline), then drag to reposition on the platform plane (constrain within radius 2.0). (2) A rotation slider (0-360 degrees) in an HTML panel that rotates the selected object around Y-axis. (3) A 'Lighting Mood' dropdown with three presets: 'Warm Showroom', 'Cool Gallery', 'Dramatic Spotlight' — each changes light colors and intensities with smooth tweened transitions over 0.5 seconds. (4) A scale slider (0.5x to 1.5x) for the selected object with real-time preview. (5) A 'Capture Angle' button that smoothly animates the camera to a predefined beauty-shot position (5, 3, 0) over 1 second, disabling OrbitControls during animation. (6) A 'Reset Scene' button that animates all objects back to default positions, scales, and rotations. Validate that objects cannot overlap (check bounding box intersection and prevent placement if colliding). Display a small status bar showing the selected object name and its current rotation/scale values. Use a dark gradient background (CSS) and add a subtle ground shadow beneath each object using a shadow-receiving plane. All UI controls should be in a semi-transparent panel fixed to the top-right corner.
